what_its_for: Zaleplon is a sleep medicine used to help you fall asleep if you have trouble sleeping (insomnia). It helps you get to sleep faster but is not meant to keep you asleep for a long time. It is usually prescribed for short-term use only (7 to 10 days).
how_to_take: Take zaleplon by mouth with a full glass of water right before you go to bed, or if you wake up in the middle of the night and have trouble falling back asleep. Only take it when you have at least 4 hours left before you need to wake up. Do not take it with or right after a heavy or high-fat meal, as this can make it work more slowly. Swallow the capsule whole.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 10 mg taken once at bedtime. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 5 mg if you are older, have liver problems, or are taking other medicines. Never take more than 20 mg in one night. Only take one dose per night. Do not take a second dose in the same night.
missed_dose: Zaleplon is only taken when you need it to sleep, so there is no regular schedule to miss. If you forget to take it before bed, only take it if you still have at least 4 hours before you need to wake up. If you have less than 4 hours before you need to get up, skip that dose and do not take it.
storage: Store zaleplon at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking zaleplon — it can cause dangerous drowsiness and breathing problems. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires you to be alert the morning after taking this medicine until you know how it affects you. Avoid taking other sleep medicines, anxiety medicines, or medicines that cause drowsiness unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid eating a heavy or fatty meal right before taking zaleplon. Do not take more than your prescribed dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sleepwalking, sleep-driving, or doing other activities while asleep that you do not remember (like eating, making phone calls, or having sex); severe confusion or memory loss; thoughts of harming yourself; allergic reaction signs such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; worsening depression or unusual behavior changes. Also call your doctor if your sleep problems do not improve after 7 to 10 days, or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Zaleplon works very quickly — usually within 15 to 30 minutes of taking it. This is why you should only take it right when you are ready to get into bed and sleep.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Start with a lower dose (5 mg) because this medicine stays in your body longer and you may be more sensitive to its effects, increasing the risk of falls and confusion. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. It may harm an unborn baby, and it can pass into breast milk. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor will prescribe a lower dose. People with sleep apnea or breathing problems: Use with caution — tell your doctor about any breathing problems before taking this medicine.
